clue.text: Piece of software to carry in fix

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, here the carrying word goes within the fixing word

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it
to lug is to carry something heavy

explanation.surface: Someone is told to bring something along in order to repair it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts LUG inside PIN, giving P-LUG-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plug-in is an add-on program that extends a host application, so it is a small piece of code.

clue.text: Lone epic changing view of historical period

indicators.note: seeing the words lone epic differently, by changing them, means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A solitary epic poem alters how we see a period of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing view of' rearranges LONEEPIC into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pliocene is a geological epoch, roughly 5.3 to 2.6 million years ago, so a period of Earth's history.

clue.text: Rude, showing everything about love, ending in debauch

indicators.note: about here means going around, so the first piece wraps the love letter

love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: ending in points to the final letter of the word debauch

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside UNCUT to make UNCOUT; 'ending in' takes H, the last letter of 'debauch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncouth means lacking manners or refinement, so it is a synonym of rude.

clue.text: I'm study engaging almost half students in deception

indicators.note: engaging means taking hold of, so the study word holds the student letters inside it

parts.note: to pore over something is to study it closely

indicators.note: half of the eight letters of students would be four, and almost half takes just the first three

explanation.walkthrough: 'almost half' takes STU from 'students', and 'engaging' puts it inside PORE, giving PO-STU-RE after I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a fraud in which someone pretends to be another person, so it is a deception.

clue.text: Carriage runs into part of tree in the morning

indicators.note: into tells us the runs letter is placed inside the tree word

parts.note: a bough is a main branch of a tree
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.walkthrough: 'into' puts R inside BOUGH to make BROUGH, then AM follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn coach with an enclosed body, named after Lord Brougham.

clue.text: Turn in blokes that have wrecked most of mother's sheltered accommodation

parts.note: to turn in is to go to bed, which is to retire
blokes is British slang for men

indicators.note: wrecked means ruined, so the letters it applies to are thrown into a new order
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: mother, read without the possessive

explanation.surface: Men who wrecked their mother's place go off to a care home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims MOTHER to MOTHE, and 'wrecked' rearranges that to THOME after RETIRE and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A home where elderly people live with some support is a kind of sheltered housing for those who have stopped working.

clue.text: Unexpected result at university? That's fixed

parts.note: in British usage a student who is up is in residence at university
set means fixed or firmly in place

explanation.surface: A surprise outcome at a university contest turns out to have been rigged.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means being in residence there, a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An upset is a surprise win by an underdog, a result nobody predicted.

clue.text: Crucial position as to the wrangling

indicators.note: wrangling means arguing, so the letters of as to the are fought over into a new order

explanation.surface: People argue about who should take the key role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrangling' rearranges ASTOTHE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The hot seat is the place of pressure and responsibility, a critical role where decisions must be made.

clue.text: Couple switching round in dance for a short while

indicators.note: a couple of letters switching round means a pair of letters, here the last two, swap places

parts.note: the minuet is a slow stately dance

explanation.surface: Dance partners change sides for a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Couple switching round' swaps the last two letters of MINUET, ET becoming TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute is sixty seconds, a brief span of time.

clue.text: Royal comment cited by hecklers?

parts.note: a famous line attributed to Queen Victoria, expressing displeasure, which a heckling crowd might quote back at a poor performer

explanation.surface: A monarch's remark is thrown back by people barracking a speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is traditionally ascribed to Queen Victoria, rebuking a courtier's joke with the royal 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria's legendary rebuke of an off-colour joke is a royal remark of disapproval that a hostile audience could echo.

clue.text: Nice pint I downed for starters!

indicators.note: downed suggests knocked over, so the letters of nice pint I are tumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a good pint knocked back as an opener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'downed' rearranges NICEPINTI into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Incipient means just beginning to appear, so it describes something at its start.

clue.text: Demo — there's something wrong about it

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the wrong word wraps around it

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IT inside SIN, giving S-IT-IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest where people occupy a place and refuse to leave, so a demonstration.

clue.text: Battleship is limited by endlessly rough weather ultimately

indicators.note: limited by means hemmed in, so the is word sits inside the rough word
endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rough treatment is cruel treatment

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word weather

explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CRUEL to CRUE, 'limited by' puts IS inside it, and 'ultimately' gives R from 'weather'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a large fast warship, so a fighting vessel of the navy.

clue.text: Hideaway for scoundrel about to be in France

indicators.note: about here means around, so the scoundrel wraps the French verb

parts.note: a rat is a contemptible person, a scoundrel
etre is the French infinitive to be

explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ETRE, French for 'to be', inside RAT, giving R-ETRE-AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is a quiet secluded place to withdraw to, a refuge.

clue.text: Indian leader's hour as guest of new European group

definitions.note: the possessive 's stands for is, so the definition is the leader himself

indicators.note: a guest stays inside a host's home, so the hour letters go inside the group letters

parts.note: EU, the European Union

explanation.walkthrough: 'as guest of' puts HR inside N plus EU, giving NE-HR-U; the 's after 'leader' is the link 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister after independence.

clue.text: Able to calculate change in menu charge

indicators.note: a change in the word menu means rearranging its letters

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Someone good with figures spots an altered price on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change in' rearranges MENU into NUME, then RATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerate means competent with numbers and basic mathematics, the counterpart of literate.

clue.text: Remainder mostly chill around study in home

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ice is a chill or freezing cold

explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts REST to RES; 'around' puts DEN inside ICE, giving I-DEN-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, a dwelling.

clue.text: Man's location is in his era, surprisingly

surprisingly signals that the letters of his era turn out in an unexpected order

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of sea between Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Promise articles about Queen (quite a few)

indicators.note: about means around, so the article wraps the queen letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

ten is a fair number, quite a few

explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives both THE and A; 'about' puts R inside THE, giving THRE, then A and TEN follow.

clue.text: That girl is married without love, displaying courage

parts.note: her refers to that girl
love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: HER, IS and M surround O, giving HER-O-ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroism is great bravery, so it is courage on show.

clue.text: Fly round lake in the sun

indicators.note: round means the fly word encircles the lake letter

parts.note: to soar is to fly high

explanation.surface: Insects buzz around a lake, basking in sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb; 'round' puts L inside SOAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to or situated in the sun, as in solar flares.

clue.text: One breaking into sequence with a certain pride?

indicators.note: into tells us the broken letters are placed inside the sequence word

indicators.note: breaking means the word one falls apart and its letters rearrange

explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges ONE to EON, and 'into' puts it inside LINE: L-EON-INE. A group of lions is a pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means like a lion, and lions live in groups called prides.

clue.text: Crazy folk mostly gas

parts.note: men are people, folk

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: gas is informal for idle talk

explanation.surface: Mad people mostly just chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like fuel but means chatter; 'mostly' trims TALK to TAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mental is British slang for mad or wildly unhinged.

clue.text: Hair not initially odd in part of lug

indicators.note: not initially means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: a beard is facial hair
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.walkthrough: 'not initially' cuts BEARD to EARD; RUM, old British slang for strange, follows. Lug is informal British for ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The eardrum is the membrane inside the ear, and lug is a colloquial word for ear.

clue.text: Bad daughter managed to have say inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the say letters go within the managed word

EG, exempli gratia, means for example, which is what say means here

explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts EG within RAN. She is one of King Lear's cruel elder daughters in Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan, with Goneril, betrays her father in King Lear, so she is one of literature's wicked daughters.

clue.text: Ill-favoured time to leave criminal dens

indicators.note: to leave means the time letter departs from the dens word

parts.note: hideouts are places where criminals hide

explanation.surface: Ugly places where crooks lurk, and time to get out of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' removes T from HIDEOUTS.

clue.text: Object, flimsy, failing at the last

indicators.note: at the last points to the final letter of the word failing

explanation.surface: A fragile item gives way in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the last' takes G from 'failing', after THIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any physical item, which is what an object is.

clue.text: Calls back uncontrolled movements in language studies

indicators.note: back signals that the calls word is read from right to left

tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics that studies meaning in words and sentences.

clue.text: Scene contrived by a Roman politician

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters of scene are put in a new order

explanation.walkthrough: 'contrived' rearranges SCENE to SENEC, then A follows.
